previous.headline: Wake-based chronotherapy is reported to improve some cases of depression
previous.summary: The article describes wake therapy combined with lithium and morning bright light as a treatment for depression, particularly drug-resistant bipolar depression. It reports rapid improvements in some patients but notes relapse after recovery sleep, practical limits, and a possible risk of mania. Other sleep-timing approaches are also being studied.

corrected.intervention: Sleep deprivation plus lithium and bright light therapy
corrected.indication: Bipolar depression, including treatment-resistant bipolar depression
corrected.headline: Sleep deprivation with lithium and light therapy was studied for bipolar depression
corrected.summary: The reported wake therapy combines repeated total sleep deprivation, lithium and morning bright light for bipolar depression, including resistant episodes. A study of 143 inpatients reported rapid symptom changes with one-month follow-up. The report notes relapse and mania risks. This combination differs from sleep-deprivation, phase-advance and light protocols that do not require lithium.

prepare.verified_regimen: The trial explicitly requires lithium for bipolar participants and combines alternate-night wake therapy with light therapy. The non-lithium unipolar cohort is not the basis for association.
prepare.note: Six previous incompatible associations remain rejected. The new trial is separate from the primary 143-inpatient study.
